---
title: "Models"
---

`lm()`, `glm()`, `lmer()`, and `glmer()` fit models with phit. phit reads
factor levels from the table, builds the model matrix from an R formula, and
fits the model. phplyr adds no model code of its own.

| phplyr | phit function |
| --- | --- |
| `lm()` | `Phit\fit_ols()` |
| `glm()` | `Phit\fit_generalized_linear()` |
| `lmer()` | `Phit\fit_mixed_gaussian()` |
| `glmer()` | `Phit\fit_mixed_logistic()` |

phit 0.4 also has the older names, such as `fit_lm()`, as deprecated aliases.
phplyr calls the current names.

The functions come from the [phit](https://github.com/phpstats/phit)
extension or from [phit-polyfill](https://github.com/phpstats/phit-polyfill),
its PHP port, and phplyr calls both the same way. phit's
[Extension or polyfill](https://phit.phpstats.org/docs/extension-or-polyfill)
page compares them. The
[Models benchmark](https://phplyr.phpstats.org/benchmarks/models) times both
through phplyr.

- Install the polyfill with `composer require phpstats/phit-polyfill`. When
  the extension is loaded, the polyfill defines nothing.
- The polyfill throws an exception while OPcache's JIT is enabled. Set
  `opcache.jit=disable` where it runs.
- `mean()`, `sd()`, `var_()`, `median()`, and `quantile()` call phit only when
  the extension is loaded. Otherwise, including with the polyfill, they run in
  PHP with the same results.
- With neither installed, the four functions throw a `RuntimeException` that
  names the missing phit function.

CI runs phplyr's tests with each implementation. Both runs compare `lm()` and
`glm()` coefficients with R's, and `lmer()` fixed effects with lme4's.
The [Models verification](https://phplyr.phpstats.org/verification/models)
lists the comparisons.

::: {.panel-tabset group="syntax"}

## PHP 8.5+

```php
$table |> lm('y ~ x + group');
$table |> glm('passed ~ hours', family: 'binomial');
$table |> lmer('score ~ hours + (1 | school)');
$table |> glmer('passed ~ hours + (1 | school)', family: 'binomial');
```

## PHP 8.3–8.4

```php
phplyr($table)->lm('y ~ x + group');
phplyr($table)->glm('passed ~ hours', family: 'binomial');
phplyr($table)->lmer('score ~ hours + (1 | school)');
phplyr($table)->glmer('passed ~ hours + (1 | school)', family: 'binomial');
```

:::

| Function | Model | Options |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lm($formula)` | Linear regression | |
| `glm($formula, family:)` | Generalized linear model | `family: 'gaussian'` (the default), `'binomial'`, or `'poisson'`, and `link:` |
| `lmer($formula)` | Linear mixed model with lme4's random-effect terms, such as `(1 \| school)` | REML by default; `reml: false` fits by maximum likelihood |
| `glmer($formula)` | Generalized linear mixed model | The binomial family with the logit link and one random intercept, such as `(1 \| school)`, which is what phit supports |

Other named arguments go to phit's function unchanged.
[phit's documentation](https://phit.phpstats.org/docs) lists them and the
formula syntax it accepts.

## Results

Each function returns phit's result array in place of a table, so it ends a
method chain. `columns` holds R's coefficient names, in R's order, and
`coefficients`, `std_errors`, `p_values`, and `conf_int` follow the same order.
The array also has the fitted values, residuals, fit statistics such as
`r_squared` and `sigma`, and `n_observations` and `n_dropped`, which count the
rows used and the rows dropped for missing values.
